newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany will not reach 96 M3 target-Buba's Issing.
newsitem.headline: Germany will not reach 96 M3 target-Buba's Issing.

text.p: Bundesbank chief economist and directorate member Otmar Issing said on Tuesday that Germany would not reach its target for money supply growth in 1996.

"In my opinion, money supply growth could slow down somewhat by the end of the year," said Issing, but he added that the Bundesbank would not meet its target for money supply growth of four to seven percent in 1996.
M3 money supply grew at a headline annualised rate of 8.4 percent in October, which was stronger than expected.

Speaking at a conference in Munich, Issing said the criteria for joining EMU required a strict and narrow interpretation and that there was no room for creative accounting by countries seeking to join currency union.
Issing said that the inflation outlook for Germany looked promising. "Nowhere in Germany is there a danger that inflation will flare up," he said.

On the issue of German unemployment, which grew to over four million on an adjusted basis in October, Issing said that even a growth rate of 2.5 percent would not be enough to reduce the number of jobless in 1997.
The German Council of Economic Experts has forecast a GDP growth rate of 1.5 percent for 1996, rising to 2.5 percent in 1997, which Issing described as "not sparkling, but definitely positive".
He added that there were still risks that Germany would not achieve these rates of growth.
